text:
emma_support: FYI customer 'Acme Corp' opened an urgent ticket — p99 latency for streaming responses jumped from ~800ms to 4.2s this morning. Non-streaming endpoints look normal. Can we triage?

ben_sre: can you paste a sample request_id + timeframe? also which client (SSE/h2) and region?

emma_support: request_id=acme-req-20260317-1123, saw ~11:20-11:28 UTC spike. Customer uses our hosted SSE path via us-east-1. They reported TTFB specifically is high (first chunk arrives late) but total tokens/time matches non-stream after first chunk.

alerts_bot: [slo-alert] tenant=acme corp p99_streaming_latency exceeded 3s between 2026-03-17T11:18:30Z and 2026-03-17T11:26:10Z — graph: https://dash.redwood.internal/slo/tenants/acme?from=11:15&to=11:30

jun_infra: we rolled out a proxy coalescing tweak last night (coalesce_window_ms=12 -> 18ms) to reduce small writes to edge. Might be related to first-chunk aggregation; SSE is sensitive.

kate_devex: quick repro steps we'll try: curl -N against streaming endpoint and compare curl without -N. Also try curl with "Accept: text/event-stream" vs application/json. Paste the exact curl you want tried.

ben_sre: repro curl I used locally:
```bash
# streaming (SSE)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-mini" -N

# non-streaming
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":50}' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=false"
```

ben_sre: captured a client-side trace for request acme-req-20260317-1123: first chunk arrived 3.9s after request start, subsequent chunks spaced ~85ms. Attached snippet from edge proxy logs:
```
[11:20:04.125] tenant=acme req=acme-req-20260317-1123 recv_from_origin=0.012s write_buffered=3.912s flush_attempt=3 coalesce_wait=0.018s
[11:20:04.126] tenant=acme req=acme-req-20260317-1123 origin_chunk=0 size=512 flush=true
```

maria_runtime: runtime side looks fine — origin emitted first chunk ~12ms after request. That suggests the proxy/edge did extra buffering/coalescing before sending the very first event.

ethan_support: customer workaround for now: they can set header X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: fast or add query param stream_chunking=immediate to bypass coalescing. We can also ask them to switch to non-stream temporarily (stream=false) if TTFB hurts UX.

jun_infra: we have a per-tenant override for coalesce_window_ms. I can set acme -> 0ms to force immediate flush for first 30m while we monitor. Will need deploy approval.

ops_deploy: approved. Patching proxy config for tenant acme to coalesce_window_ms=0 now (canary to edge-3 then all). Rolling out to edge-3 @ 11:35 UTC.

ben_sre: after canary on edge-3 I reproduced locally with same token against edge-3: first-chunk latency dropped to 18ms. Data: before 3.9s, after 0.018s. That confirms coalescing change is culprit.

kate_devex: action items for customer comms: (1) explain root cause concisely (edge coalescing increase impacted small first-chunk writes), (2) short-term: we toggled immediate flush for them, (3) ETA for global fix / revert. I'll draft message.

jun_infra: long-term options: revert global change, make default window smaller for SSE clients, or add heuristics to detect origin-first-chunk and bypass coalescing for first byte. We'll schedule design sync with runtime + proxy.

maria_runtime: prefer heuristic: if origin reports a small first-chunk and connection is SSE/h2 streaming, bypass coalesce for chunk 0. That avoids perf hit for other workloads that benefited from coalescing.

ethan_support: customer confirmed improved UX after our toggle at 11:36 UTC. They saw first chunk consistently under 100ms.

emma_support: marking ticket as "partial fix applied - monitoring". Will follow up with customer and reopen if we see recurrence. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops_deploy: note: will keep tenant override active for 1h then rollback to previous config; file a runbook to reapply per-tenant override if needed.

ben_sre: follow-up: write a quick perf test we can run in CI to simulate different coalesce_window_ms values (0/5/15/25ms) and measure streaming TTFB p50/p95/p99. I'll open a PR.

kate_devex: also adding a short blurb to streaming FAQ explaining how coalescing affects TTFB and recommended headers/workarounds for integrators.

emma_support: customer message sent, closing thread for now. If anything else pops up I'll reopen.
